title: Heads Will Roll – Soberanía 129
author: Mexico Solidarity
content:
In episode 129 of Soberanía, hosts José Luis Granados Ceja and Kurt Hackbarth
discuss the arrest of former Chihuahua Attorney General César Jauregui on
suspicion of treason, after an investigation found he may have allowed CIA
agents to take part in an irregular raid on a suspected drug lab — a case that
only came to light because the agents' vehicle fell off a cliff and exploded.

Next, they dig into an El Financiero poll showing Morena at 46% of decided
voters ahead of the 2027 midterms, with the PAN at 8%, the PRI at 6%, and
Movimiento Ciudadano reeling from the Guadalajara repression. They unpack the
junior parties' fight for survival and the irony that Morena needs those
troublesome allies to hold its two-thirds majority.

The conversation then widens into the Mexican-American vote in Texas, where
early voting shows a striking swing, and how Trump's indiscriminate
immigration crackdown has shattered the Republican dream of splitting
documented and undocumented Latinos — with the death of Emiliano Andrade
Covarrubias in an ICE detention center as a case in point.

Losers and Haters takes aim at the FBI, which rejected journalist Joseph
Heffernan's FOIA request about the El Mayo Zambada kidnapping by citing
"personal privacy" — even as the plane used in the operation sits on display
at the War Eagles Air Museum in New Mexico, complete with photographs and
technical data.
